title: Rootless: `podman exec` and healthchecks fail with crun 1.31 when the container's oom_score_adj was clamped
body:
> **Note:** I investigated this and wrote this report with help from Claude, Anthropic's AI assistant. That covers finding the cause, reading the Podman and crun sources, and drafting the text. Every reproduction and measurement below was run on my machine.

### Issue Description

When rootless, Podman clamps a requested `oom_score_adj` that is lower than its own up to its own value (#19829, #19843), and logs:

    Requested oom_score_adj=0 is lower than the current one, changing to 200

The clamp is applied in `generateSpec` to the spec the container starts with ([container_internal_common.go#L845-L851](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/v6.2.0/libpod/container_internal_common.go#L845-L851)). But `prepareProcessExec` builds an exec session's process by copying `c.config.Spec.Process`, which still holds the unclamped value ([oci_conmon_exec_common.go#L686-L689](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/v6.2.0/libpod/oci_conmon_exec_common.go#L686-L689)).

Up to crun 1.30.1 this was harmless, because crun did not apply `oomScoreAdj` on exec. crun 1.31 does, as its [release notes](https://github.com/containers/crun/releases/tag/1.31) say: "exec: inherit rlimits, I/O priority, scheduler, memory policy and oomScoreAdj from the container configuration, and apply the oomScoreAdj of the exec process". An unprivileged process may lower its `oom_score_adj` only down to `oom_score_adj_min`, the value last set by a privileged process. With systemd's defaults the user manager is set to 100 and the user's processes run at 200, so the floor is 100. Any requested value below that floor makes every exec into the container fail, including healthchecks.

docker-compose, through the Docker-compatible API, sends `OomScoreAdj: 0` for every container. Podman stores 0, starts the container at 200, and execs at 0. So under systemd's defaults every compose service with a healthcheck becomes `unhealthy`, and `docker compose up --wait` fails. Reading podman's database for such a container shows `oomScoreAdj: 0` in the stored spec, and the started spec has 200.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Rootless, with crun 1.31, on a systemd host with its defaults (the user manager at oom_score_adj 100, the user's processes at 200). Use 0, as docker-compose sends:

1. `podman run -d --name oomtest --oom-score-adj 0 docker.io/library/postgres:18 sleep 300`
2. `podman exec oomtest true`

The container starts, with the clamp warning. The exec fails.

On a host whose floor is 0 or lower, 0 won't reproduce it. Use `--oom-score-adj -1000` there instead, as Podman's own clamp test does: that is below any unprivileged floor. On the host above, a value from 100 to 199 still works and 99 or below fails, matching the user manager's 100.

The same exec run with crun 1.30.1 succeeds. Running the identical exec process spec (`oomScoreAdj: 0`) with `crun exec --process` directly shows the difference too: 1.30.1 succeeds and 1.31 fails.

### Describe the results you received

    Error: crun: write to `/proc/self/oom_score_adj`: Permission denied: OCI permission denied

The exit status is 126. A container created this way with a healthcheck reports `unhealthy` with empty healthcheck output.

### Describe the results you expected

The exec succeeds, and the exec process gets the same clamped value as the container's process (200 here).

### podman info output

    Podman 6.2.0, rootless
    crun 1.31 (fails); 1.30.1 (works)
    conmon 2.2.1
    Kernel 7.3.3 (CachyOS, Arch-based), amd64
    cgroups v2, systemd cgroup manager; systemd 262
    Docker Compose 5.7.1 against the podman API socket

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

None beyond the above.

### Additional information

A possible fix: apply the same clamp to the exec process in `prepareProcessExec`, or store the clamped value so that exec copies it. Until then, a workaround is to request an `oom_score_adj` at or above the user's current value (for example `oom_score_adj: 200` in the compose file).
